correctness.rationale: For every real h>0, three-line cyclic itineraries of length three have two possible orientations, and length four either alternate on two lines or repeat exactly one of the three lines. Alternating two-line projections have only the intersection as their possible periodic point and do not follow a nonconstant farthest-choice itinerary. Each remaining affine return has a unique candidate. The two period-three candidates have strictly positive winning squared-distance differences exactly for 1<h<sqrt(3+2sqrt(3)). The base-repeated period-four candidate has strict branch conditions exactly h^4-h^2-1<0, while the unique candidate repeating either sloped line must take a projection from a base point on the wrong side, or is a fixed-point tie at h=1. All admitted cycles have distinct nonvertex points in the edge interiors. The multipliers (1-h^2)/(1+h^2)^2 and 1/(1+h^2)^2 have modulus below one, so the cycles are locally attracting. Standalone Fraction-based itinerary enumeration passed 488 exact assertions at 111 rational heights. Finite checks corroborate but do not replace the universal projection algebra.

originality.rationale: The journal and lawful arXiv full text of Everett establish the farthest-projection map, generic convergence claims, and qualitative isosceles bifurcations. Neither states the exact four-cycle parameter cutoff, the exclusion of four-cycles repeating either sloping side, or the coexistence window. The closest previously published mathematical result, whose full RESULT.md was read, completely classifies primitive three-cycles on the same full-line system and explicitly excludes other periods from its scope. Its period-three criterion is credited and does not imply the new four-cycle admissibility comparisons. The new result is a full first-eligible-even-period classification and a sharp cross-period coexistence statement, not a rewording of the period-three classification. No stronger overlapping result was identified in actual multi-query published-finding corpus and primary-literature searches. Priority remains provisional outside inspected evidence.

value.rationale: Four is the smallest even length that can visit all three nonparallel supporting lines; alternating on only two cannot produce a genuine nonconstant cycle. Exhausting its three repeated-line itinerary types produces a complete natural low-period classification and an exact golden-ratio geometric cutoff, not an arbitrary parameter slice. The unexpected stable coexistence of distinct least periods is an invariant dynamical feature that the qualitative asymptotic-periodicity theorem and the previous three-cycle census do not determine. The result locates precise bifurcation boundaries and local multipliers without claiming larger periods or basins.
